text_fidelity_a:
Echo Buds (1st Gen) – Wireless earbuds with immersive sound, active noise reduction, and Alexa I’m updating my review because I ended up returning them after several frustrating runs.

I wanted these for exercise but I got fed up after 1) the connection to my iPhone would drop 2) when running they would start to come out of my ears even with many different variations of the ear-wings and the inserts and when you touched them to push them in the touch features would activate 3) Alexa was hit or miss. I would be running on trails where there really was not much noise, but she didn’t always respond to voice commands

So I bought these about two weeks ago at full price and when I logged in to leave this review imagine my surprise to see them at 40 dollars less. Honestly, even at 40 less they are quirky. Sometimes Alexa answers but sometimes you have to say her name several times. I also have trouble when I am jogging out in the woods as it seems like Alexa has to have the WiFi instead of being able to use a cellular connection. As such, if I want to change songs I have to use my phone instead of hands free. In addition sometimes songs just stop for no reason.

The sound is good but I still don’t think it is too much better than the 40 dollar no name versions I have had in the past. The fit is good but that is due to having so many options for both in ear bud and ear wing. (And since I usually use these when working out I bought these because they had an ear-clip/wing option to keep them in.)

I believe these are ok for a first generation Alexa integrated war bud option, but just like Alexa for my car, I think I should have waited for the next generation.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Buds (1st Gen) – Wireless earbuds with immersive sound, active noise reduction, and Alexa

text_fidelity_a:
Canary Pro Indoor Home Security Camera 1080p HD WiFi IP | 24/7 Watch Live Video, Siren, Climate Monitor, Motion Alerts, Two-Way Talk, Night Vision, 10x Zoom, Private Mode, Works with Alexa and More Doesn't live up to the hype. The image quality is not great unless you're right in front of the camera. I placed mine on the tv console, which is on the far side of the room, and has the best views of the living and high traffic areas. You know, where you actually want surveillance...

First unless someone is within 3 feet of the camera, you can't make out faces.

Second the time delay between canary detecting movement and notifying me of activity has been 15 and 30 minutes, including when I've been in the house. When I was out of state, the delay was 15 min. When I was in my own home but in night mode, the delay was 30 min. So I'm not sure how this would be effective in notifying the police because it would give robbers plenty of time to clear out your house before you even see it.

Third you need to be aware of the location you place it and the natural shadows that occur throughout the day. I was getting notifications every 10 minutes. So I changed the sensitivity, but I still get notifications.

I think the concept is great, but the technology has a long way to go.
text_fidelity_b: Canary Pro Indoor Home Security Camera 1080p HD WiFi IP | 24/7 Watch Live Video, Siren, Climate Monitor, Motion Alerts, Two-Way Talk, Night Vision, 10x Zoom, Private Mode, Works with Alexa and More

text_fidelity_a:
WiFi Mp3 Player with Bluetooth, TIMMKOO 4.0" Full Touch Screen Mp3 Mp4 Player with Speaker, Portable HiFi Sound Walkman Digital Music Player with FM Radio,Recorder, Ebook,Clock, Browser (White) Ok, first of all, I want to say I LOVE this player much more than others I've used. My kids are not allowed cell phones in school, but they are allowed music players- however most players that aren't smart devices are really janky with buggy/slow UIs and lots of impairments (I tried encoding a video for one and it wouldn't work unless I used a very archaic codec that required a suspicious Chinese desktop app). This, however, actually runs a stripped down version of Android under the hood. This is a GOOD thing! The UI is very polished and smooth thanks to open source mature OS, and features like video playback are much more robust with a wider variety of formats supported and compatible as a result as well!
The hardware is smooth and the menus are intuitive thanks to being familiar with the Android OS already. It's a very cute device!
So why only 3 stars? Well, the listing claims it has a web browser and FM radio. Both of those things are missing on this model. The truth is, I don't need my kids to have that anyway, but it feels weird that the listing advertises features which aren't there. I think I may have gotten a different model than the one advertised.
I considered side-loading a browser apk since it DOES run android, but the truth is this isn't designed for that sort of use and wouldn't make a difference for the purpose of this review. I'd imagine that there are a lot of possible hacks and modifications possible thanks to the operating system inside if someone wanted to tinker.
text_fidelity_b: WiFi Mp3 Player with Bluetooth, TIMMKOO 4.0" Full Touch Screen Mp3 Mp4 Player with Speaker, Portable HiFi Sound Walkman Digital Music Player with FM Radio,Recorder, Ebook,Clock, Browser (White)

text_fidelity_a:
JVC HAECX20B Sports Clip Inner Ear Headphones, Black The sound quality of these earbuds AKA headphones is excellent. They are exactly what they are advertised to be, earbuds with clips that go over the ears to keep them from falling out of your ears when you are engaged in activities that cause a lot of moving and shaking of your head, which would dislodge ordinary earbuds.

I don't personally engage in sports that strenuous, but but I did thoroughly test these Sports Clips by bending over, hopping up and down and generally moving my head a lot. They did not come loose from my ears.

I found another excellent use for them as well. When I have normal earbuds plugged in when I am baking bread or other dishes that get my hands very messy, all too frequently non-clip earbuds begin to slip out of my ears. Its a real pain to have to wash sticky dough off my hands and dry them before I can stuff the loose earbuds back into my ears. I don't have that problem at all with these Sports Clips earbuds, and that's very convenient.

The one flaw with this product, at least it's a flaw to me, because it doesn't make any sense and is somewhat uncomfortable, is the way the cord is designed. It is not coequal in length on both sides. One side is about four times longer than the other. There also isn't any sliding plastic piece that allows you to adjust the length of the splitting of the cord so that the user can adjust how wide it gaps over one's throat and chest, which would allow the user to opt, as desired, to even tighten it right up under the chin.

Other than those issues, this is an excellent product.
text_fidelity_b: JVC HAECX20B Sports Clip Inner Ear Headphones, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Display Port to HDMI Converter with Audio Adapter I wanted to hear and see Skype on our Sony XBR7 HDMI-only capable 1080p TV, fed from a Lenovo X220 convertable laptop/tablet running System 7 64 bit Ultimate through the DisplayPort. I also wanted to watch some YouTube videos playing from Firefox and hear their audio on my big living room audio system. No such luck.

When first plugged in, I remember briefly seeing the TV via this DisplayPort adapter in the audio device list, but the next time, the TV disappeared and is nowhere to be found. Not in the audio control panel, anyway. It's just gone.

I first chalked this up to the Thinkpad weirdness, as its internal audio card/mic doesn't work with Skype either. If I plug in an external Logitech webcam, it works seamlessly. Internal camera/mic, nothing.

Sony audio problems aside, the video looks great on the big screen, though it overscans a bit and cuts off part of the menu bar at the bottom.

One reviewer said he could see his TV in the list of audio devices and was able to configure its audio to satisfaction. My Sony TV does not show in the Lenovo audio devices list, though it does show as a generic PnP monitor.

I plugged the HDMI cable into a tiny 7" video monitor and whatdayaknow, the audio came through and the device showed up as an audio device. Then I plugged it into a 20" Vizio and sure enough, it works fine too. Same with a Samsung LCD. Three monitors out of four work. The Sony is the only one that doesn't. Hmmmm.

Sooooo, I'm guessing there's something about Sony's DRM or some other HDMI protocol blocking the computer from seeing the TV. I set all the TVs for internal speakers. Routing audio to an external amp is another variable in the equation.

Nothing wrong with the adapter that I can tell, it simply doesn't see certain Sony TV's.
text_fidelity_b: Display Port to HDMI Converter with Audio Adapter

Unfortunately, the case is where the excitement ended. Pairing is simple, just pull them out of the case. You can use these together or just one at a time. These are really small but they actually stayed in my ears and that’s also while I slept. They are also pretty comfortable. The battery life is awful. They had a straight playtime at 3 hours and 20 minutes. I need the battery to last at least 9 hours and that’s really not difficult to do. I have a few earbuds that last 3 times that and at half the price. Next would be the sound quality and that was also an epic fail. If the volume would have gone past the highest aloud the bass would have been a bit better. If you need to make or receive any calls, these will definitely not work. Every time I tried to use the phone features, the call would drop right after the hellos. The distance between these and my phone were was the only thing I found to be exceptional. What a shame. Clearly the manufacturer put everything they had into the case design so that consumers, like myself, would run out and buy them, only to be disappointed.

HomeScreen (3 Minute Setup) Touchscreen Dual Band Wireless Router/Range Extender AC750 (802.11ac) I received this as a review sample and even though I am experienced with setting up and configuring networks, this was so easy that I honestly believe anyone can set it up with the scant instructions.

My initial set up was to connect it to my DSL modem just to check it out. Although the instructions are terse, you do need to read them regardless of level of experience. For one thing, it requires you to completely power off your broadband modem. For another, it takes a bit to boot up no matter how you intend to use it. Connecting to broadband was a snap.

What I really wanted was a range extender and this was as simple to configure for that as it was to configure for broadband. In that mode, when you first power it on and boot up it takes over a minute and you may be tempted to think it's broken. Don't. Once it is powered up, like the broadband set up (DSL or cable), the wizard makes it simple to discover your wireless router, connect to it and extend the range of your network. My wireless router turns in a weak -70dB from my master bedroom (measured with [[ASIN:B004EBZX6W Wi-Fi Analyzer]]) and once I installed this in the same room the signal dramatically improved to a strong -40dB. In the same room with my master wireless router this comes in at -47dB while the master router measures in at -56dB. That indicates that the signal of this router is exceptionally strong.

There are options for adding sensors for home control. I did not test that set of features because I did not receive sensors, but it is functionality that makes this router/extender a great choice if you do want to pursue home control too. There are IOS and Android apps that can be used in conjunction with the sensor features. Again, I did not explore those and probably will not since I am not interested in them. As a router alone I love this, and especially the overall signal strength and ease of setting up and configuring.
text_fidelity_b: HomeScreen (3 Minute Setup) Touchscreen Dual Band Wireless Router/Range Extender AC750 (802.11ac)

Razer Opus Active Noise Cancelling ANC Wireless Headphones: THX Audio Tuning - 25 Hr Battery - Bluetooth 4.2 & 3.5mm Jack Compatible - Auto Play/Auto Pause - Carrying Case Included - Midnight Blue I was so excited to receive these headphones and give them a go. I’ve spent right at a week with them and this is what I’ve found.

There are little to no instructions regarding these headphones and I had to research the app that has to be downloaded and go to the Razer website to begin using. Once I had everything set up, it was easy. I would have rather had a semblance of instruction than the wild packaging. The headphones were easy to pair to my phone and the sound is crystal clear. I was impressed with the noise cancelation especially. As an audiophile, I am very, very critical of sound and what is missing with these headphones is any kind of upper volume range or bass. For the price, I would have expected better in that department.

The strongest plus to these headphones is the clarity of the music. Even with the lower volume and the lack of bass, the music is sharp and clear - something I have found gets lost with other brands. The noise cancellation is also a strength above others.

Overall, I would recommend if you’re not searching for heavily bassed or volumed headphones.

It feels great in the hand and the texture is perfect. Just 1 big problem. I'm a bit of a claw grip, and this mouse provides nothing on the right side to grab onto. When I try to lift the mouse to move it around (I like having a little lower sensitive at work as well) my figers slip down the right side. It's hard to describe but there's no lip on the right side like there is on other logitech mice (even their M100 mouse has more to hold onto) It looks like there's a lip on the right but it's really not deep at all and my fingers struggle to keep it from slipping when I'm picking up the mouse.

It's also slightly front heavy but I don't find that to be much of a problem. I've learned to live with it, I grip it a little harder when I lift, and I turn on mouse acceleration (because I'm not gaming with it) and everything else works so well it's hard for me not to use it even though there's this one glaring issue. Maybe you're luck will be different.

text_fidelity_a:
ZyXEL 300 Mbps Wireless N Access Point, Ethernet Client, Universal Repeater, and Range Extender (WAP3205) Overall this is a good little feature-rich device but use just the wireless access point features. It was quick to setup but was definitely a time that you wanted to read the fine manual (RTFM (PG version)). It wasn't as easy to setup as the CISCO WES610N that I purchased at the same time BUT it is also feature rich.

I have had it up for a few days and haven't experienced major problems with it. We will see if it stands up to the test of time and gives me 3-4 years of service like my Cisco Linksys devices that are still working 4 1/2 years later.

Nerd Alert - I am a nerd at heart and utilize geek speak way too often. I try to remember that the Amazon audience contains friends, family, and strangers that may or may not know IT.

PROS:
* Feature Rich -
The ZyXEL is 1/2 the price of the comparable Cisco device but it has a much more feature rich set of wireless capabilities. It supports WPS, allowing for easy setup. It supports WDS, allowing you to configure a network that allows you to carry your laptop from room to room in a large house without sacrificing much speed if setup correctly. It can access as a repeater if needed.

* Cabling -
The ZyXEL includes the power supply and a network cable (CAT-5). It supports a standard called MDI/MDIX, which means that you won't need a crossover cable if you connect it to a switch.
* Wireless Distribution Service -
You can make this part of your existing network using WDS, or Wireless Distribution Service, or simply configure it as an access point. I just removed two old Linksys routers from being WDS nodes since replacing my old Actiontec 802.11a/b/g with an Actiontec 802.11b/g/n wireless router. Eventually I will get around to using the ONI port and setting up a network with DD-WRT

CONS:
* LAN ports on the back are are 10/100 -
While the router notes that it supports connection speeds up to 300MbPS it only has two (2) 10MbPS/100MbPS RJ-45 (LAN) connections. Technically you may never truly realize the full throughput available with this device. This is not unlike other wireless access points, such as the Cisco WET610N (single 10/100) or the Cisco WES610N (quad port 10/100 for $10 more). I did what any good geek would do; used it as an excuse to purchase an 8-port Netgear 10/100/1000 switch to replace my 5-port 10/100 switch in my office/lab with the computers and Hyper-V lab systems. I am going to use the Cisco product downstairs with my home server and VMWare ESXi box.

* Setup may be difficult for the average home user -
I most certainly RTFM'd and reading the manual helped. It did take a quick configuration of my network card in order to even get to the point I could setup the device.
The Cisco devices use an APIPA address, which makes setup easier. Why? APIPA is that 169.254.#.# address that your computer gets when it connects to a network that doesn't give out addresses. This allows you to easily setup the Cisco WES610N.
text_fidelity_b: ZyXEL 300 Mbps Wireless N Access Point, Ethernet Client, Universal Repeater, and Range Extender (WAP3205)

text_fidelity_a: (2011 Version) Instant Immersion French Levels 1, 2 & 3 I'm terrible at learning languages. I studied French in junior high, high school and a few years in college, but I still had trouble speaking French fluently. I went to Paris a few times and even dated a French native who criticized every word I attempted, so I gave up. Despite this history of failure, I was curious to see if this Instant Immersion French kit would work for me. The box claims that it is just as good, if not better than Rosetta Stone because they refuse to spend as much on advertising. Hmm. I have a hard time believing that advertising is a main reason why Rosetta Stone is popular. The set comes with 4 CDs and the instructions recommend starting with the Ipod audio CD, though the same sheet of instructions say that it should be used as a supplement to the software. As I sampled each disc, I found that the set is really designed less for a serious French student than for a traveler or someone visiting France on business. There is no attempt to teach grammar or language structure, like present or past tense. The lessons all stress memorization and the ability to recognize and parrot standard phrases, remember a good amount of vocabulary (though not the context to use it). I was disappointed to find that it is structured more like a Berlitz language course. Using flashcards and games to learn language is nothing new, and the Oscar Lake game included is absolutely ancient, as I remember this game from 1998. The only "new" thing about this immersion program is the fact it offers an Ipod and interactive DVD option. The interactive DVD was fun to use though the video is low-tech. Also, the quizzes didn't work that well - I had to click my DVD remote arrow buttons several times before it registered my choice. Did all this it work for me? Did my ability to pronounce words improve? So-so. While I enjoyed playing the games and had fun refreshing my memory using the interactive DVD, the kit offers no real revolutionary way to learn language. It all depends on the student and how motivated you are. In that case, I'd probably do well with Berlitz if I'd only tried harder.
text_fidelity_b: (2011 Version) Instant Immersion French Levels 1, 2 & 3

I tested this speaker paired with a Sony android phone. Bluetooth pairing was instant. While I didn't quite get a full 30 foot range, I found the actual 27 foot range to be acceptable.

I like the carabiner feature for hanging the speaker, from a tent ceiling, tree, or post. But I don't see anyone hanging the speaker off a backpack. The weight will cause it to swing wildly. In fact it's heavy enough to be stored in the bottom of your pack.

Recharging was easy, but the rubber plug takes a little finesse to put it back into place.

The sound was crisp with somewhat deep bass undertones. I didn't expect this little speaker to pump out heavy bass, but it's adequate for its size.

I don't recommend that you crank this up too loud when camping in the woods. The loud music might drown out the sounds of an attacking bear or wildebeest.

For the money it's a decent wireless speaker that will survive most outdoor adventures.

Samsung Galaxy Tab Pro 12.2 (32GB, Black) There are more than enough helpful reviews, product specs and Q&A, so I am going to focus on this tablet for folks who are upgrading from another Android tablet, and especially another Samsung. I'll say up front that the biggest reason [for me, anyway] is the extra screen real estate and resolution.

I had a small surprise in that mine did not come with Amazon apps pre-installed like they did on my [[ASIN:B00D029NNA Samsung Galaxy Tab 3 (10.1-Inch, White) 2013 Model]] that it replaced. Locating the App Store application so I could install all of the applications that I have purchased was a bit of a hassle, but I finally got that resolved. Like my older Samsung tablet this one is a little less than spectacular when it comes to streaming music to a speaker via bluetooth. I do not know why Samsung cannot get it right on tablets because I have never experienced any issues streaming on my Note II and Note 3 phones.

Another issue of which you need to be aware is this tablet is thin and flexible. I knew that in advance and purchased a [[ASIN:B00KCDBD2E Samsung Galaxy Note Pro 12.2-inch Case Cover]], which in my opinion is one of the better cases for this tablet. The hard shell part of the case into which you insert the tablet provides a rigid casing that allows zero flex. No matter which case you ultimately select I strongly recommend that you get one.

You may have issues with some apps if you opt to install an SD card to expand your storage, or if you are moving an SD card from another tablet to this one. The KitKat version of the operating system will not write to SD cards under certain conditions. There is a free fix called SD KitKat Fixer by JRummy Apps that you can get from the Play Store. I highly recommend it. As a side note, I had no issues with this SD card: [[ASIN:B00N2ROG9O PNY Turbo Performance 64GB High Speed MicroSDXC Class 10 UHS-1]]. It is an inexpensive way to max out your memory. I have heard that this tablet will work with 128GB cards, but I have not tested any so cannot say for sure.

If you are accustomed to Samsung's user interface you will feel right at home. For me, after the little challenges I mentioned above I was fully up and operational on this tablet in a few hours. A lot of that time was reinstalling purchased apps from Amazon and the Play Store, tweaking my settings so that they mirrored those on my Tab 10.1 (which are identical to my Note 3 phone), and this feels as comfortable as an old shoe. A much larger old shoe to be sure, and it's incredible how much extra screen space you get going from 10.1 to 12.2.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Galaxy Tab Pro 12.2 (32GB, Black)

The sound quality is good, I’ve been using them with music and streaming shows, and I haven’t been disappointed with the sound quality.

I’m not as pleased with the short battery life, touch controls, and lack of audio cues.

I get about 2-3 hours of playback per charge. It’s rare for me to battery drain earbuds, but with this pair, I hear the low battery chime every time I use them.

The touch controls and lack of audio cues go together. The touch controls are super easy to activate on accident. More than once I’ve taken the earbuds out only to find I hit Play while doing so, and they kept playing music. I also activate random controls when adjusting the earbuds in my ears … and I don’t always know what I’ve done. Did I turn ANC on or off? The audio cues are just beeps, not an announcement like “ANC on/ANC off.”

I like the design of the case. It has a sliding top, so you can actually clean the entire area where the earbuds sit. When you put the earbuds inside the case, a light flashes to show their battery level. The case charges wirelessly or via USB-C. There’s only one LED light on the outside of the case, it’s easy to miss when you’re trying to see if the case is charging or not.

text_fidelity_a:
StarTech.com StarTech.com 1-Port 10/100 Mbps Parallel Network Print Server - Fast Centronics Ethernet Printer Server Adapter - Windows 10 (PM1115P2) Customer service is 6 stars

I certainly would love this product if we could have gotten it to work. I'm on a 5GB wifi network, and the StarTech is for a 2.4GB network. It won't work with my Internet speed. Or so both my techie, Brian, and I thought. Keep reading.

However... I couldn't connect the print server (that's the little white box) with my laptop. I had a problem and got online to get it fixed. The chat tech was very polite, patient and knowledgeable, but pointed me to the support page that gave me step by step how to set up my wifi print server. Went there. Followed the steps but I had no idea what the server IP address was. Gave up until I could call and get someone to walk me through it. A survey came up asking for my thoughts on my experience. I told them I was having a problem and just needed to know what my server IP address was so I could set up to print from my laptop. Got an email from a supervisor asking if I'd like a more experienced tech to call me. Yes! I would.

Got a call from Brian. He was very helpful, patient, and walked me through everything. Then I had to let him have remote control over the process because it got too complicated for me. That's when we discovered that the print server wouldn't work with my internet speed. So I told him how grateful I was for his patience and help even though I couldn't use the thing that was going to save me so much time. We hung up and while I was typing up this 6-star review of StarTech's great tech support, Brian called me back and said he was pretty sure he'd figured it out. I gave him remote control again, and 15 minutes later I've got my wonderful wifi printer!! I'm so elated! It works.

I have Windows 10 OS on my Dell Inspiron laptop, and an HP J4540 printer -- 2008. They are now friends and talking to each other wirelessly.

I do not recommend anyone that does not know what they are doing to install this device themselves. I know a lot about computers, but I know when I need an expert. Brian is an expert! Installing the thing is complicated. If your wifi is 2.4GB, then you can follow the instructions on the website most likely without a problem. If you have a higher speed Internet, then there's a lot more backdoor stuff that needs doing. I have a feeling they'll be updating the instructions on the website for this kind of problem. But if you have any problems, contact StarTech tech support. They are the greatest this side of the sun... no joke!
text_fidelity_b: StarTech.com StarTech.com 1-Port 10/100 Mbps Parallel Network Print Server - Fast Centronics Ethernet Printer Server Adapter - Windows 10 (PM1115P2)

text_fidelity_a:
Nikon D3100 DSLR Camera with 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 Auto Focus-S Nikkor Zoom Lens (Discontinued by Manufacturer) First, let me preface that I in NO way count myself a photog. I am just a shutter bug who has been firing frames almost non-stop since the age of 18. I learned on my dad's 'old' Nikon SLR with an f/1.2 lens. The Nikon SLRs/DSLRs I have owned are: N50, N60, N55, N80 and D50. My N50 ad N80 had the best lenses. The N60 and N55 were not as great and the D50 was a fabulous entry-level digital. The only medium format camera I own is my Holga. But hey, unlike the photographer at Portrait Innovations, at least I know 'medium format' does not refer to the number of megapixels at which I am shooting. As for my working knowledge, I had three semesters of photography in college. I can process/print both B&W and color film. (Not that that does me any good these days LOL) I can shoot completely 'manual' and I have stood among many pro photographers on the bridge at sunset, waiting for the color to be just right on Half Dome. (My Bogen tripod was way too heavy to be practical for an amateur but it gave me street credit.) So, in a nut shell, I shoot by the 'Sunny 16' rule. I know that opening my f-stop should increase my shutter speed give me a shorter depth of field; and, per the great Ansel Adams, f/8 is a proper exposure for all pictures.

That said, I hate my D3100.

I have had metering issues since I opened the box. I bought the camera so I could take 'even better' pictures of my infant son than I was getting from my D50. Ha. Joke was on me.

The contrast was BLINDING on the factory settings and every shot was over exposed. I have tried every metering option in the menu but the only changes I can achieve are under-exposure, blurred focus and missed shots. It's go high or go without.

I always lower my ISO to 100 when I'm outside because I crave rich color but it's just not there. I have tried Aperture Priority, Shutter Priority and Manual. Nothing. f/16 over my film speed on a sunny day. That's supposed to work! I have used it on many a 'less complicated' camera and achieved photos that make jaws drop. Well, there's no jaw dropping with this camera.

The metering overrides my manual choices every time. It's like I'm having a battle of wits with my camera. :( It reminds me of the days when Kodak was marketing 800-speed film as a universal, never-miss-a-shot solution to all your photo woes. Bleh. Just because there's always an image doesn't mean it's the RIGHT exposure.

I get that being an entry-level/made-for-the-masses DSLR really does mean it's a glorified point-and-shoot but it should preform at least as well as it's predecessors. Honestly, I got far more reliable results from my Canon SureShot and a roll of Kodak 100.

My expectation for a camera is that the image should be very close to perfect when the shutter closes. I know there's always room for improvement before printing but that's the art of photography. The hours I spend working on my photos after the shot should be to make them pop. Instead, my time is spent trying to rescue precious memories.

If you are considering this camera as your first DSLR because you think it will improve your skills, skip it. Invest in an equally expensive point-and-shoot that will give you all the same manual controls and preform much better in low-light situations. The D3100 does not live up to the standards of a Nikon SLR.

I gave it a second star because my son pulled mine off the counter about a year after I bought it and although the case cracked, it didn't seem to hurt the camera. Unfortunately, it impact didn't help it, either. (Yes, I was actually hopeful.)
text_fidelity_b: Nikon D3100 DSLR Camera with 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 Auto Focus-S Nikkor Zoom Lens (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

LotFancy Laptop Cooling Pad with 2 LED Fans Ultra Slim Portable Chill Mat for 13 to 15 Inch Computer, Dual USB Ports I received this as a free review sample and it was sorely needed because the internal fan in my ThinkPad T61 finally died. Note: if you are looking at this as a cure know that many laptops report a fan failure then shut down. In the case of mine, I found that I could press the On/Off button briefly when that happened and it would power back up and boot Windows.

This fan array moves a lot of air, promoting excellent heat transfer. So far it has worked well and I have had no premature shutdowns (although I still have to go through the On/Off button sequence every time I power the ThinkPad up.)

Do be aware that this fan array will interfere with other USB peripherals if you power it directly from your laptop, and especially if you add even more peripherals to the ports integrated into this unit. That is because the power draw form USB ports may exceed the capacity of the laptop, especially if you are running it off an unpowered USB hub. I had that problem when I tried running this, a mouse and a speaker from my laptop. I moved this one to a powered hub and the problem was immediately resolved.

Also, this raises a laptop 1 3/8 inches higher at its lowest setting. For me it took a day to become accustomed to the raised typing height, but since it solved a genuine problem the tradeoff was worth it. Just know that you will need to adjust to that and it may slow down your productivity for a day or two.

If your laptop has a fully functioning internal fan this array will augment that and keep your laptop cool even in unairconditioned spaces on a hot day. That will definitely prolong the life of the internal electronics and the hard drive.
text_fidelity_b: LotFancy Laptop Cooling Pad with 2 LED Fans Ultra Slim Portable Chill Mat for 13 to 15 Inch Computer, Dual USB Ports

text_fidelity_a:
PreSonus C3.5 BT Channel Studio Monitor I have been wanting to get a bluetooth speaker for connecting to my tablet for a while so I was very pleased to get an opportunity to try this speaker set. It is far and away better than what I originally had in mind and so far I am more than pleased with them.

Setup of these speakers is straightforward and simple, so much so that instructions really are not needed to get started. The wire connector is color-coded to make connecting the speakers to each other almost completely foolproof. If I have any complaints about the setup it would be that the wire connector is a little on the short side but that’s an easy fix - just buy longer wire.

I enabled bluetooth on my tablet, told the speaker set to make itself available and the tablet connected to it immediately. One could not ask for anything simpler. The process took less than a minute and most of that time was spent walking across the room to press the bluetooth button on the speakers.

I loaded up Pandora and told the tablet to play and almost immediately it was clear that these speakers are far above average. The sound profile is stunning - clear and crisp highs, rich midrange and very satisfying bass without overdriving. These speakers do an outstanding job of accurately reproducing the sound. On the back of the main (control) speaker there are two knobs for adjusting the highs and lows should the middle be unsatisfactory for some reason. These speakers also do a good job with spacial elements and there is depth to the sound.

I paired the speakers with my laptop (once I powered off the tablet) as well and it was also very easy.

I took some cables and wired the speakers to an older television in the house to see how much better watching TV would be. It was definitely better and it have a more spacial and stereo sound experience but with our TV this prevented us from making any volume adjustments unless we turned the volume knob on the speaker itself. This is a minor nuisance but certainly not a real issue.

In addition to great sound, these seem to be well-build and rugged, a good sign right out of the box. These are an excellent choice for a home theater system or an audiophile's listening room.

So far I have found nothing about which to complain with these speakers. Set-up is a snap and the sound quality is just amazing. These are speakers for the serious listener.
text_fidelity_b: PreSonus C3.5 BT Channel Studio Monitor

Diamond Multimedia 300Mbps 802.11n Wireless Repeater Range Extender with Wireless Access Point and Wireless Bridge Device (WR300NSI) This wireless range extender was fairly easy to install. The directions were straight forward, and the device was up and running in less than fifteen minutes. It comes with an CD, but we didn't have to use it. We did have to reset the IP address on the computer, but that may have a user issue and not related to the device itself.

It took a little while to find the best place to plug the device in based on our home's layout, but we found one that worked. In our house plan, the best place ended up being in the hallway at baseboard level. Fortunately, the device is small and plugs straight into the wall, eliminating any unsightly cords. It would have been nicer to have the device a little more out of the way. We were a little concerned about this thinking it might get kicked or knocked by the kids as they race around and play. That hasn't happened yet, but it is something to take into consideration if you have small children or pets around. We tried placing it in a less open area hoping to protect it a little more, but none of those areas produced a satisfactory result.

It's very easy to tell how much of a signal the device is receiving from the main router. Three bars is full signal, and one is low signal. The signal indicator light is easy to read and is quite bright. Since the device is in our hallway, it acts as a nice night light and would be rather distracting if it were in a bedroom.

The end result: the dead spots are gone. We can use all of our devices in the those areas without having to worry about losing a signal.
text_fidelity_b: Diamond Multimedia 300Mbps 802.11n Wireless Repeater Range Extender with Wireless Access Point and Wireless Bridge Device (WR300NSI)

Wacom Bamboo Splash Pen Tablet (CTL471) Just a few days ago I finally decided it was time to give my old Genius 8x6 MousePen up. It was time to upgrade to a Wacom. I browsed for a day or two trying to decide what would best suit me, and after a lot of thought I decided this would be the tablet I purchased. It arrived the earliest day it said it would arrive, and that was a treat.

After I opened it up I thought this tablet would be too small since my other one was a bit bigger, but I tested it out in one of the programs that came with it, ArtRage Studio, and was very surprised. I barely realized the drawing space was small, and it was very comfortable and felt very natural to be drawing on. The tablet itself does not take up much space at all, and it's very light and small enough to be easy to work around. ArtRage Studio is also a very nice bonus. It's a great alternative to Photoshop and other programs (I actually see myself using this program more than my Photoshop). The Splash also came with three spare pen nibs for when your current one wears down.

The pen is also very nice in that it doesn't use batteries, and it also fits comfortably in your hand.

I am a little disappointed that this isn't compatible with a wireless connection, but the cord on the tablet really isn't that obtrusive.

I'm very happy with my very first Wacom product, and I hope I can upgrade once more in a few years.
text_fidelity_b: Wacom Bamboo Splash Pen Tablet (CTL471)

Sony X90J 50 Inch TV: BRAVIA XR Full Array LED 4K Ultra HD Smart Google TV with Dolby Vision HDR and Alexa Compatibility XR50X90J- 2021 Model , Black After almost 3 weeks with this television, I am amazed and very, very happy with it. There's a lot to like here and a couple of things that I wasn't expecting from any television.

First is the ease of set up. Our previous smart tv was a ROKU and reasonably simple to set up as well. The Google connection here means just signing in with your existing Google info and the tv uploads your existing apps. Just like moving to your new Android phone or tablet. All of our streaming apps populated and we were able to sign in without drama - HBOMAX, Prime, Paramount Plus, HULU and Netflix. We only stream and haven't used cable or satellite in 5 years, so easy app access with a new tv is important.

The 4K picture is outstanding. There's no distortion in picture quality or digital noise even from old 1940s movies. The colors are rich and full and the tv settings let you adjust to your preference as well. We've watched a lot, A LOT of tv recently and every show on all platforms has been gorgeous. Frankly, we probably watch way too much tv as a rule and that's not going to change. I've been amazed at the picture quality difference between our year old HD tv and this one.

We've connected Alexa to this tv and the voice controls work...most of the time. Using the voice control via the remote control renders better responses for sure. The tv has recognized a Fire stick, Roku Express stick, and a portable DVD player for us without any drama. We don't have a gaming system, though.... I'm considering buying one for this giant screen.

But my final show stopper moment with this television has been the sound quality. We've never had a tv that didn't require a sound bar. Until now. Despite the tv being quite thin and lightweight, the speakers still produce a deep sound quality without any tinny undertones. The settings have a calibration option for the speakers that you definitely need to do for the best sound - it works. I truly believe this is the best television we've ever owned.
text_fidelity_b: Sony X90J 50 Inch TV: BRAVIA XR Full Array LED 4K Ultra HD Smart Google TV with Dolby Vision HDR and Alexa Compatibility XR50X90J- 2021 Model , Black

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Paperwhite E-reader (Previous Generation - 7th) - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi) with Built-in Light, Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity - Includes Special Offers For years, I used the keyboard kindle after it first came out and loved the "classic" look of the page so much. After replacing it several times due to screen issues, I finally made the switch to the paperwhite with some skepticism, thinking the back-light would make it into yet another screen I look at. I was pleasantly surprised that even the brighter settings still look like a page, and I can turn it all the way down for the same effect as my older model kindle. Plus, I don't need to bother anyone with a light anymore when I read in bed, in the car at night, etc.

Paying a bit extra for no ads was worth it, and I enjoy the drawings that serve as screensavers. The home page is not my favorite - I would prefer to default to my library list instead of wading through recommendations, etc. - but it's not that much of a hassle to tap over to the library screen. When I'm reading a book, it automatically opens to the page I left off on just like my old kindle.

I only vaguely miss having the 3G function my old kindle had because I used to live out in the boonies with limited internet access. However, the WiFi has been generally sufficient and now I just make sure I download a few books before I travel.

Overall, the kindle has definitely revolutionized the way I read since it first came out when I was in high school. I do still keep a lot of hard copies of my favorite series and enjoy reading real books from time to time, but the kindle is SO easy to download anything, anytime you want. Not to mention bringing a whole library with you in one slim package while traveling! I have had this model for a year and a half now, and have no issues or complaints at this time.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Paperwhite E-reader (Previous Generation - 7th) - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi) with Built-in Light, Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity - Includes Special Offers

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st) I have an iPad and an HP Touchpad, but the Fire has quickly turned into my favorite tablet for entertainment activities. The reasons are simple - it makes it incredibly easy to access movies, TV shows, books and magazines from Amazon, many of which are free under Prime. I can hold it for hours without it getting uncomfortable, the screen is great, and the overall look and feel of the operating system is intuitive. Storing and accessing content on the Amazon Cloud is also a seamless, simple process.

I was concerned about the screen size since I've become used to the larger tablet screen sizes of the iPad and Touchpad. I'm finding that the benefits of a smaller screen size (easier to hold in one hand and light weight) outweigh most of the disadvantages. I miss a larger screen the most when I'm reading a magazine or a newspaper, but the copy remains highly readable even on the smaller screen.

Sound quality is decent with the onboard speakers. Nothing spectacular but workable. I find a decent set of headphones/earbuds to be a worthwhile addition. The touchscreen is also not without an occassional glitch. I get the same "lack of a final polish" feeling using this as I do with my Touchpad versus the more slick feeling of the iPad. But none of these issues impact usability, and I'm willing to let some factors slide in exchange for a more affordable price.

Is it an "iPad killer" or an "Android tablet killer"? No. But why is that even an issue? I wanted an easy way to avail myself of the benefits of Prime membership (most notably being able to stream shows and movies for free) and the Fire accomplishes this very well. It comes at a price that's a lot easier to handle than the iPad, and a level of ease of use/functionality that's easier to handle than Android tablets.

None of the so-called limitations of the Fire detract from my using it. Yes it has limited onboard storage but with the way the Cloud is integrated, I've not had any difficulty using that as a way of storing content. Plus, when Amazon stores it, they deal with the issue of backup. I also don't miss the 3G connectivity. Sure, I'd love to be able to connect anywhere, but I will not pay the prices charged for data connectivity. I never use the 3G on my iPad for the same reason - just costs too much!

I'll certainly keep and continue to use my iPad since I use that a lot for work. But when I'm done with work and want to have fun, the Fire will be in hand. It's cheap, works well, and provides access to virtually unlimited video and print entertainment. For me it's a perfect fit.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st)

text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm Finepix F70EXR 10MP Super CCD Digital Camera with 10x Optical Dual Image Stabilized Zoom and 2.7 inch LCD This is a high quality camera, but you must take time to read through the owner's manual to understand how to get the best pictures. You can just grab it and point and shoot using it while in the "automode" setting, but the resulting pictures may leave you a little disappointed depending upon the photographic conditions. To get the highest quality photos you must become familiar with how this little beauty works. Unfortunately, you might have to print out and tote the manual with you when you find yourself in situations where your pictures aren't what you'd like, or you can't figure out how to do certain things like know what's behind the flashing icon error message, or how to simulate different types of film, or can you choose between clarity, reduced noise and dynamic range? This is not really a simple "point and shoot" camera and all images will turn out great. You will have to study it, practice with it, and most of all have patience and you will be pleasantly rewarded for your efforts. Though the indicators vary with camera settings, there are 23 different indicators just for shooting mode, and 12 for playback mode, not to mention the date/time stamp, battery level, and indicator. It can get confusing.

Although a basic manual booklet is included with the camera, a much more detailed manual must be uploaded from the enclosed CD and then all 125 pages can be printed out or read from your computer monitor. The manual covers all the material in the booklet almost page for page but includes much more information about features the booklet leaves out and the booklet will refer you to specific pages in the manual for more information. Also, in the manual are about 50 FAQ's that are very useful. I am a manual reader, (having written many technical SOP's) and appreciate having well-written and well thought out manuals that are understandable and succinct. Though I would have preferred a manual that I don't have to upload to my computer, it is well-written and many useful pictures are included.

This camera is loaded with many different options/features but accessing and understanding many of them will require reading the manual. For people who don't want to be bothered with all the bells and whistles this camera may be more than they need. I can see very serious photographers using this camera. Reading through the manual I have compiled a list of some of the various modes, options and features available:

Digital Zoom
Movie Mode
Silent Mode
Variable ISO settings
Image size selection
Aspect Ratio selection
Intelligent Face detection
Scene Position
Shooting Modes
EXR Mode
Film simulation
Dynamic Range
White Balance
Continuous Photography
Photometry - multi, spot, average

Playback Options:
Erase
Slide Show
Red-eye Removal
Image Rotation
Protection from accidental deletion
Crop
Resize
Voice Memo
Print Order
Time Difference
Format

Pages 37, 67-68, 86-87, 97-103, and 104-107 would be good to print out and keep with your camera as they contain tables of various camera functions and a trouble shooting chart.

I have taken many pictures and movies inside and out, light and dark, with this camera set on various settings. And though I have practiced with it now for several weeks, I still need to often refer to the manual when I choose to vary from automode. Some things I have found especially desirable are:

Silent Mode - I attend classical music concerts where flash photography is prohibited. This mode will silence all beeps and flashes.

Large viewing screen on the back of the camera. It is exactly 5.5cm x 4.0 cm.

Digital Zoom - extremely good. I attended a local minor-league baseball game and sat far away on the grass well beyond the playing field. I was able to fully zoom and still get good, clear, close-up shots of the players with no blurring.

Movie Mode - Completely surpasses any other I've experienced so far. Images are clear, colorful and the sound quality is excellent. Camera noise was heard and recorded while using the "zoom" function in Movie Mode though it was not very loud.

Multi-frame play back function is very useful to quickly scan for a particular picture.

Fine Pix Viewer Program was very easy to install on my computer. I use Windows XP.

Very good photography in low-light conditions.

Also some things I did not find particularly desirable but are not major flaws:

I cannot directly burn a CD using the Fine Pix Viewer Program which comes with this camera. I have to use another camera program, import the pictures into it and then burn a CD.

Very easy to accidentally turn it on or off and easy to get misfires.

The zoom lever is too sensitive. I have learned with practice to barely move it very slowly.

The camera does not give helpful suggestions on how to get a better picture as does my HP R717.

Not HD capable.

The higher the ISO the grainier the picture though a higher ISO is desirable when shooting in dim/low light levels. I have set the ISO level to 200 and that seems to produce the best pictures so far.

Almost too many options, modes and functions to choose from. Though you can immediately begin to take pictures using Automode, it will take time to fully understand the many other aspects and features this camera has.

In Summary:

I can find no major complaint concerning this camera. It takes excellent clear and colorful photos even in situations where I least expect it - indoors with no flash. Any poor quality pictures I have taken are not the fault of the camera but due to the photographer's ignorance of how to use/understand properly the many features of the camera. The basic mechanics of such things as battery and memory card installation are very easy. Battery charging is a very simple process and battery life seems long. The manual is detailed and covers more than I would probably care to know. This is almost more camera than I need, though I will continue to use it and will update this review as necessary.

UPDATE 2.9.15 - Been using this camera all these years and now it's beginning to show it's age and giving me some problems. The viewing screen on the back has a vertical big black bar but it doesn't appear on the actual pictures. And the lens cover doesn't always completely open when the camera is turned on. I still use it but it might be time to think about a replacement. It's been good though so I really don't have any complaints.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm Finepix F70EXR 10MP Super CCD Digital Camera with 10x Optical Dual Image Stabilized Zoom and 2.7 inch LCD

text_fidelity_a:
Jabra SPORT Bluetooth Stereo Headset - Black/Yellow (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I am disappointed with these headphones for only one reason: My ears are small, and because of that, these headphones will not snuggly "hang" over my ears like they should. (Children would have the same problem, I expect.) If the over-ear part of the headphones were a little more moldable, I might be able to make them work for me; the extra ear gels themselves are helpful in getting a good fit into the ear canal, but that doesn't keep them from falling off of me. This is why I'm knocking of a star but, again, the problem is not with the headset but with my own anatomy!

With that caveat aside, I love them! For a gardener who wants to listen to something outside while working, the FM radio works just fine and the yellow rubbery cord keeps them around your neck even if you do knock them off. The U.S. Military-grade protection features (against dust, moisture, and shock) make these headphones stand out from the pack.

The Bluetooth pairing and sustained connection with these is better than any other Bluetooth device I've ever used, although I tend not to use Bluetooth unless I'm up and about in the house doing chores. I also don't make or get a lot of phone calls, so we don't even have a cellphone account and depend on the occasional VoIP to get the job done. Meaning I haven't tested the headset features at all.

But the sound is crisp and clear, without mud, more like monitoring headphones used in the music industry. I feel no pressure when wearing them (holding them to my head with my hands, of course, to keep them from falling off of my teensy ears), and I know they would be very comfortable for me in daily use. Maybe I can come up with something to rig them with so they don't fall off. Because I really do like them.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra SPORT Bluetooth Stereo Headset - Black/Yellow (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

We previously purchased both a series 2 aluminum and series 1 aluminum and returned both. Really wanted the stainless sapphire combo without spending a lot. We considered these nice toys. We both have Rolexes and the sapphire lens is virtually indestructible. Our Rolexes went into the jewelry box as these Apple smart watches are both useful and enjoyable.

These are not toys. Extremely useful watches. Great features. Use Siri to make calls off your contact list. You don't have to type the number on a tiny screen. On the walking track, or while walking the dog, glance at your watch if a call or text comes in. Don't have to fumble with the phone while holding a leash. Have the music icon on the Watch face. It allows me to activate and change songs or albums without pulling my watch out. Have the calendar on my watch face. Quick glance each morning keeps me from forgetting about appointments. Weather icon also on my face. Tap it twice and it goes from current temp to 10 day forecast. Activity monitor on face lets me track my steps without having to pull my phone out.

All in all, an extremely useful item.

Disregard all early reviews. The updates make the original gen watch an extremely useful item. And a fun toy to boot.

text_fidelity_a:
Foldable Bluetooth Keyboard, Geyes Folding Wireless Keyboard with Portable Pocket Size, Aluminum Alloy Housing, Carrying Pouch, for iPad, iPhone, and More Tablets, Laptops and Smartphones(Gold) This folding keyboard is a bit of a betwixt and between product, but if it is the sort of thing you think you might use, then it’s got a lot to like about it. If you have a tablet (and my experience is with iPads so keep that in mind), then their built in keyboard is a better choice for short work just because it’s larger and more natural to type. For longer work, the choice will be more individual in that some people hate writing for extended time on the hard surface of a tablet keyboard and others don’t mind at all. I can do a pretty long stint and for really long work, I’ll shift over to a Bluetooth keyboard, either Apple’s own or a smaller Logitech one that also acts as a cover. I’d prefer both of those to this because again, they are larger and so more comfortable.

When one considers the keyboard as a phone accessory, then things change a bit, and this become a much more viable choice. If I have to do any halfway extensive typing on a phone for work (something beyond texting, an email or two, etc., then this would definitely be my preference over the phone itself.

1) it takes up very little space (and comes with a nice little pouch). Tossing it into a backpack is nothing, but I could easily fit it into a coat pocket, a cargo pants-like pocket, keep it in my car console without it blocking much space. None of which would be true for my wireless Apple keyboard or even my slimmer Logitech one. The additional “bulk” is therefore relatively negligible.

2) the typing is quite nice on it. I was pleasantly surprised at the key travel, the ease, the tactile sense.

3) It’s definitely small and a little cramped, but not so I notice it unless I’m typing for a long time (half hour or more) and then I just need to take a few minutes break. The small size doesn’t come into play too often. I had to readjust to the apostrophe, and one has to hunt and seek a bit for less-used keys, but that’s easy enough and once you’ve been typing for a while it becomes just as second nature as normal typing does. And it’s much faster and much more comfortable than extensive phone typing

4) the stand is a nice little touch that works quite well, placing the phone at a usable and pleasant working angle and letting you sue it in both portrait and landscape mode.

5) I haven’t exhausted the battery so can’t speak to how long it will go, but it’s certainly lasted a good number of hours, more than I’d ever use it for (if I’m working that long I’m going to my laptop or tablet)

6). Build quality seems sufficient. I wouldn’t say it feels highly durable, but nor would I call it cheap feeling or overly flimsy. And when it’s folded I have no concerns about it breaking.

All in all this was actually quite the pleasant surprise and again, if you would ever find yourself needing to use your phone for that sort of mid-range work (more than you’d want to do on a phone keyboard but not so much you’re turning to a laptop) then I’d highly recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Foldable Bluetooth Keyboard, Geyes Folding Wireless Keyboard with Portable Pocket Size, Aluminum Alloy Housing, Carrying Pouch, for iPad, iPhone, and More Tablets, Laptops and Smartphones(Gold)

In other words, assembling, mounting and adjusting this can be done by one person. My mount shipped with thumb style bolts and optional, heavier ones that you can use with the included hex wrench. Since my monitor was so light to begin with I used the thumb bolts, which hold the viewing angle in the narrow range of movement the VESA mount allows. Had my monitor been heavier I would have probably used the hex bolts, which are a lot beefier.

Bottom line: read some of the other reviews that discuss challenges that this mount has for heavier and larger monitors. However, if you have a 24" that is in the 10-12 pound range (or less) this is all the mount that you need. It's built like a tank, is a breeze to assemble, and holds lighter monitors absolutely rock steady.

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Oasis E-reader (Previous Generation - 9th) – Graphite, 7" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Waterproof, Built-In Audible, 32 GB, Wi-Fi - with Special Offers (Closeout) I purchased one of these 9th generation Kindle Oasis. The first unit I received would freeze during the configuration process. You could reset it, but if you try to configure, it would freeze again. At this point, I made the mistake of asking for a replacement instead of just returning the faulty Kindle Oasis for a refund. A replacement unit arrived in three days. Unfortunately, the replacement unit was DoA. There was a fixed image on screen, and I wasn't able to get a response from this Kindle after charging it for a long time and multiple reset attempts. I had already shipped the first unit back using a UPS shipping label created by Amazon at this point. I went to my Amazon Orders page to return the second unit for a credit. But Amazon web interface wouldn't allow a self service return for refund. I had contact customer service and deal with several customer service representatives. They consistently asked me to try some simple trouble shooting steps ( most of which are not even applicable if you have a completely dead kindle). They wouldn't listen to me when I said I just wanted to return it, and try to pressure me into another replacement. At this point, I had spent several hours troubleshooting, talking to Amazon Customer service, taking packages to UPS, etc. so I insisted on a return for refund. This time, the customer service representative said he was having problems generating the return label, and then disappeared. After several minutes of wait, another customer rep took over and worked on this case for another 10 minutes or so. At that point, I ended up with two sets of return labels in my email. The customer service rep told me to use the labels from the second email (in chronological order). So the next day, I shipped the replacement Kindle Oasis back. A few days later, I saw on UPS tracking that the package was delivered to Amazon and three days after this I received an email confirmation from Amazon that my first return was received. A few days later, I saw on UPS tracking that the second Kindle Oasis (replacement) was also received by Amazon. I waited a few days for return confirmation and refund from Amazon, but nothing happened. When I contacted Amazon Customer service, they kept telling me that I shouldn't worry about getting charged as my replacement is complete. But they could see no record of my return of the replacement. I spent probably a good half an hour chatting with a customer service rep but they couldn't help me at all since they could only see the record for on return request. That chat ended with no resolution because I ran out of time and had to get to an appointment. Later, I got in touch with yet another service rep, and explained everything from scratch. Luckily, that person was able to find records of both returns being received by Amazon and finally issued me a refund.

So lessons from this story:
1. Don't buy a 9th gen Kindle Oasis. There seems to be serious quality control issues. The probability of one customer receiving two faulty Kindles in a row would be infinitesimal unless fault rates are in the 20% range.
2. If you receive a faulty Kindle from Amazon, return it for a refund. Don't ask for a replacement. Amazon's automated return process cannot handle the return of a replacement unit, and you will sink a lot of time dealing with customer service representatives
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Oasis E-reader (Previous Generation - 9th) – Graphite, 7" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Waterproof, Built-In Audible, 32 GB, Wi-Fi - with Special Offers (Closeout)

text_fidelity_a:
KINESIS Freestyle2 Ergonomic Keyboard w/ VIP3 Lifters for Mac (9" Separation) UPDATE 1/5/14: I'm downgrading my rating of this keyboard to three stars for one main reason: there are very sharp edges on the inside of the two sides of this split keyboard which can cut your wrists if you aren't careful. I put my mouse in between the two sides of the keyboard because that is the best position for it for me to prevent back and arm strain. Unfortunately, every time I use the mouse, my right wrist runs into the sharp edges of the inside of the right side of this split keyboard. To give you an idea how bad this sharpness is, I wear a [[ASIN:B008C27UPQ sport wristband]] to protect my wrist, and it is literally shredding from coming in contact with the knife-sharp plastic edge. I have tried putting duct tape over the sharp edge, but it won't stick to the plastic this keyboard is made of, and to add insult to injury, the tape looks awful.

Previous Review:

I recently had a bad flare-up of right arm pain from repetitive stress. I experimented to figure out which movements at my computer were hurting me the most, and I realized that reaching for the mouse was even more painful than keyboarding. As a result, I searched for keyboards here on Amazon with the potential to be divided in half, so that I could place my mouse right in front of me. That search led me to this keyboard.

This "freestyle" keyboard gives you the option to either leave the two sides hooked together and place it at a 45-degree angle on each side, or unhook the two sides totally. It is a simple procedure, no tools required, to unhook the two sides.

This product comes with instructions for putting the keyboard together from scratch, but everything came assembled except for mounting the padding that supposedly goes under your wrists--I have medium-sized hands, and the padding lands at the base of my hands, nowhere near my wrists. The padding also is not very thick, and I'm not sure why the manufacturer did not just go ahead and paste on the padding themselves--it's a hassle making sure it is totally straight before you stick it on. It can't be re-positioned if you mess up. Fortunately, I didn't mess up, and I don't have a huge need to support my wrists, so I am not downgrading my rating for that, but some consumers might want to know about it.

I really like the ability to put my mouse pad in between the two halves. This works as well as I had hoped to prevent the strain of reaching for the mouse constantly. The keys have a nice feel to them, as well. I am a touch typist, and I was very concerned at first that I would lose that ability on a strange keyboard. I have learned after multiple long days of using the keyboard that the trick is to get my fingers in the right position to begin with, such that my right pointer finger is on the J, and my left pointer finger is on the F. Even so, I currently hit false keys much more than normal. I hope that time and use will overcome this issue. I have ordered an additional one of these keyboards to hook up to my laptop so that I am always employing the same keyboarding reflexes, in order to more quickly retrain my brain.

This keyboard is certainly much more expensive than the $15-19 keyboards I've used forever, but will be well worth the price if it, as I think it will, helps prevent the excruciating pain of repetitive stress syndrome.

This keyboard is made so that the inner section can be elevated at either of two selected heights, or it can be fairly flat. This is useful for varying the position of the hands. As a physical therapist told me years ago, changing position and resting are crucial for preventing repetitive stress. I've tried all three levels, and I find the highest one the most comfortable.

Another plus of this keyboard is that I can now bilaterally employ a beneficial PT suggestion: I have for years placed a pillow under my right arm which is positioned against the arm of my [[ASIN:B000PWGZOI rolling office chair]]. This takes the strain off my arm and shoulder by bracing them. The fact that I'm using a pillow means that I am not in danger of damaging the brachial plexus nerve in the axilla (underarm), which can happen with hard objects like crutches. Previously, it never felt comfortable when I used a traditional keyboard to do this for my left arm, but with this keyboard, it does. Now, with both arms/shoulders braced, I find that it is much easier and even automatic to keep my back straight and my head up. It has greatly eased not just arm and hand strain, but back, shoulders and neck strain as well. In addition, I make a point to take my hands completely off the keyboard and mouse when reading, vs. keyboarding, and the pillows give me a comfortable place to elevate my hands, on the top of the pillow where it extends from beneath my underarm.

I rate this product as follows:
Ease of use: 4 stars (should improve with practice)
Functionality for preventing muscle strain: 5 stars
Comfort of use on wrist: 3 stars
Ease of assembly: 4 stars
Attractiveness of keyboard: 4 stars
text_fidelity_b: KINESIS Freestyle2 Ergonomic Keyboard w/ VIP3 Lifters for Mac (9" Separation)

Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combos, Cnacnoo Full Size Slim Keyboard 2.4GHz Silent Mouse with Nano USB Receiver Multimedia Keys for Windows, Laptop, PC, Notebook Free OTG Cable for Android Tablet Phone As an old, retired guy I spend a lot of time online gaming, streaming videos, and dabbling on social media. Over the last few months I've tried out a variety of keyboards and mice, some of them high end gaming gear. As soon as you take this keyboard and mouse out of the box it's clear that this is a low end rig. It just doesn't have the solid heft of more expensive equipment. That's not necessarily a bad thing though as I've used some excellent, inexpensive keyboards and mice. Sadly, this product is not of that caliber either.

The compact size makes the keyboard feel cramped when typing. Even as I'm writing this, my fingers are feeling strained from the cramped tightness. The manufacturer makes the 12 function/F key combos seem like a big deal. To me those combos just seem like an unnecessary complication. There are other, more standard ways of doing all those things without having to learn a whole new set of keys. The six "hot keys" seem to be just a set of video controls that duplicate functionality already available on any computer with a standard video player.

The mouse is particularly disappointing for anyone who does gaming. Now I'm just a casual gamer, by no means a hard core one, and even I find this mouse to be a handicap. In my main game you move your character forward by holding down both the left and right mouse buttons simultaneously. With other mice that is no big deal. With this mouse there is a perceptible hesitation or stutter before moving when holding down the buttons like that. That may not sound like a big deal to a non-gamer but that kind of stuttering can quickly get your character killed in a gaming battle. Also, it seems to take some effort to hold those buttons down. My fingers feel a strain in holding these mouse buttons down, a strain I haven't felt with other mice. And yes, I did try the suggested solutions for mouse problems offered in the "Manual" that came with this product (one tiny sheet printed on both sides). They didn't help.

So if you are mostly watching videos and reading Facebook on your computer, you will probably be okay with this gear. Any more serious use than that and you will want to pass on this stuff.
text_fidelity_b: Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combos, Cnacnoo Full Size Slim Keyboard 2.4GHz Silent Mouse with Nano USB Receiver Multimedia Keys for Windows, Laptop, PC, Notebook Free OTG Cable for Android Tablet Phone

text_fidelity_a:
Apple AirPods Pro Long story short I lost my airpod pros. Saw these on major discount ($90 for Black Friday), and couldn't resist. So here's my take in four parts. Sound Quality. Noise Cancelling. Ambient pass through. Features.

Sound quality -- versus the airpod pros, these are almost identical in sound. The only difference is the beats buds are a touch bass heavy. It's good, punchy bass, but noticeably more than the pros which were more balanced with its lows. So if you're a bass head, or hip-hop enthusiast, the beats win hands down.

Noise cancelling -- now this could have to do with the shape of my ear, but I found the beats to actually be a step ABOVE in noise cancelling. My gf still has her airpods and I compared. The seal the beat creates, paired with its noise cancelling makes it seem like the world doesn't exist. Beats win for me in NC.

Ambient pass-through -- this is where the beats lose out. Their noise cancelling is too good. So even when you have transparency turned on the world sound a little muddied out, while with the airpods, if I had transparency on it was almost like I wasn't wearing them. I miss that alot. So if you are in an environment where you need to hear what people are saying without removing your buds then airpods might be your pick. It's not to say that beats mak you deaf or anything but things are just noticeably quieter in transparance vs airpods with its full clarity.

Features -- another loss for the beats. They don't work with the beats app so no equalizer function... why beats???? WHY?? So you'll have to go third party if you want to equalize. The beats also won't stop the music or video you're watching if one falls out. No biggy for me as I like that but some people might not. Other than that it has similar functionality to airpods. One click to pause, two to skip, etc. It doesn't auto switch between devices but does actually switch pretty similarly. Takes maybe two clicks to switch it to my mac. The pairing is a breeze with iphones. Just open the case next to your iphone and voila. It's paired.
text_fidelity_b: Apple AirPods Pro

text_fidelity_a: Jensen CD-555 Pink CD Bluetooth Boombox Portable Bluetooth Music System with CD Player +CD-R/RW & FM Radio with Aux-in & Headphone Jack Line-in Limited Edition (Pink) I was looking for a portable CD player to use in my van which didn't come with one. I also wanted one that was simple to use and didn't have a lot of fancy features. I ordered a different player and wasn't happy with it and ended up returning it. Although this player had some negative reviews I thought I'd take my chances to see if I like this one. It isn't as portable as the smaller one I returned, but I'm extremely happy with it. It now sits on my kitchen counter and I listen to the local radio station every day and I wasn't even looking for a CD player with a radio feature. I haven't tried the bluetooth feature yet and not sure if I will. The radio and sound are great and you can really crank it up loud which I couldn't do with the first player I tried. I like the carry handle which makes it so easy to transport from room to room and the fact that it can be used with batteries. The only negatives I see with this CD player: (1) the size is a bit larger than I wanted but this enables it to have larger speakers and better sound quality doesn't it? (2) I would like it to be USB rechargeable instead of having to be plugged in and (3) the color claims to be red but it is more pink than red (when everything else I own is real red, this is a bit irritating). Overall, I am happy with this Jensen CD Player and will not be sending it back.

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Aspire R 15 2-in-1 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 7th Gen Intel Core i7, GeForce 940MX, 12GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, R5-571TG-7229 Wow, before saying anything, the screen on this laptop is stunning; bright and sharp. It is not the first nice thing I noticed about the laptop. Out of the box, it has a solid, perhaps a little heavy feel. It has a matte crosshatched finish which is not my favorite, but looks classy enough. The basic shape is elegant, it is thin and sleek and satisfying in the hand.

Keyboard/Touchpad

The keys are backlit, crisp to the touch and typing is easy. It has a slightly compressed full keyboard with a squeezed 10 key which is nice, and at least for my uses fine that the keys are 2/3rds their normal width. Keypad is sensitive but clicking works better than most and I have no problems with fine control of the cursor. The fingerprint reader is on the touchpad but does not affect usage and is a nice touch in general. All in all, inputs through keyboard, touchpad and touchscreen are perfect.

Screen

Like I said, once this one on, the screen is what stuck out for me. Wonderfully bright and crisp. Touch screen controls seem to work fine. Screen size is great. We watched a number of HD nature films on it and felt comfortable. The screen hinges completely around to create a tablet which I far prefer to swivel options. I also liked the way that it tents for movie and presentation viewing. Could not be happier with the screen.

CPU/Performance

This is a nice quick machine. SSD, i7 and plenty of RAM out of the box had it booting quick and I see no problems with performance. I would be amazed and happy to see it approach the 9 hours of battery life that it promises, we'll see about that over time. My son wanted to put it through the paces with STEAM games but I'm passing - It's mine, but it should handle most reasonable games although it is obviously not optimized for hard core gaming.

Summary

This is a well built, solid laptop. It has the makings for a great Netflix platform with it's screen and flexibility of viewing positions of the screen as well as crisp, bright HD. This is hands down the best laptop I have owned as a complete package.

Pros
+ Super Bright, HD screen
+ Nice crisp feel to the keyboard
+ Well powered for standard uses, SSD, i7 and RAM gives it enough muscle

Cons
-The design of the power cord and jack are disappointing, It looks spindly and its design encourages lateral pressures. I really wish more thought went into that.
-The pattern on the outside is not my favorite, but looks nice enough
text_fidelity_b: Acer Aspire R 15 2-in-1 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 7th Gen Intel Core i7, GeForce 940MX, 12GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, R5-571TG-7229
